summary: The only new untrusted input is the `observed` field of session records read from IndexedDB, which a tampered profile could change. Path: IndexedDB value -> findPausedSession/parseSessionRecord -> observedField -> restoreObserved -> useTableSession ref -> countObserved/userObservedSnapshot -> advice worker. Validation fails closed and does not coerce. A non-array is rejected. A sparse slot or non-object entry is rejected before any property is read. botId must be in the set built from the record's bot seats, which are already checked to be safe integers in 1..nextBotId-1, and it must not repeat. hands must be a whole number in 1..handsPlayed (handsPlayed is capped at MAX_SESSION_COUNT), vpipHands in 0..hands and pfrHands in 0..vpipHands, all via Number.isSafeInteger. Prototype keys: restoreObserved only writes keys that passed that botId set check (positive integers), so `__proto__` or `constructor` can never be a key. Huge arrays: the duplicate-id check means a valid array can hold no more entries than there are bot seats (at most 9), so the loop throws by index botSeats+1 at the latest. A sparse array with a huge length throws at the first hole, so its cost is bounded. Error message echo: messages hold only the fixed field path and a small integer index, never stored values. The existing console.error logs only the RangeError. hands >= 1 means later ratio maths never divides by zero. restoreObserved re-runs parseSessionRecord and sits inside App.resume's existing try/catch, so a bad record falls back to the no-resume path. The write side serialises only counts the app computed itself. There are no new dependencies, randomness, secrets or network use. No findings.
